newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-Brussels bourse rises on merger mania.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brussels bourse rises on merger mania.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, booming on the back of a wave of mergers and speculation about more alliances to come, hit record levels on Monday.
The Bel-20 index of 20 blue chip stocks pushed to a record 2,273.79 points during morning trade, up from Friday's close of 2.267.78.
Among the big gainers were holding companies Almanij and Cobepa.
The two firms announced plans last Friday to share out the assets of holding company Gevaert in a move that puts pressure on other holding groups to simplify their structures too, analysts said.

Speculation remains rife about alliances in the financial services sector. Some analysts say these are still needed, despite news on Friday of a merger between the country's seventh and eighth largest banks, non-listed Bacob and Paribas Belgium.
Bank Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL), up 4.42 percent at 9,450 francs, was the biggest gainer in the Bel-20 -- which does not contain any of the stocks involved in Friday's announcements.

The prospect that BBL could soon find itself with a new owner has risen again on reports one of its main shareholders, Belgian insurance company Royale Belge, is about to be sold to Dutch financial services group ING. ING has declined to comment on the reports.
ING already owns 20 percent of BBL, the result of a failed 1992 takeover battle. It has so far used that stake to block a merger between BBL and Belgium's biggest bank, Generale Bank.

If ING bought Royale Belge it would immediately acquire another 12 percent of BBL and possibly more, as Royale Belge shareholder, Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, might also sell its own 12 percent BBL stake.

Royale Belge is expected to be questioned about its future at its annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday. Its controlling shareholder, French insurance group AXA-UAP declined to comment on Friday's reports.

Kredietbank also firmed on Monday, rising 1.6 percent to 14,425 francs on top of the 3.27 percent gain made on Friday following news the bank was holding exploratory talks about an alliance with Dutch Rabobank.

News of the Gevaert/Almanij/Cobepa deal also spilt over to some of Belgium's other holding companies, which make up more than half the listings in Brussels. Shares in Brederode, a market darling for months, had risen another 4.55 percent to 4,600 francs by midday.
Brederode has made no secret that it too is considering simplifying its group structure, which includes five other listed holding companies.
"The (Gevaert) deal as a whole is very good for the Belgian market, which has always been pressured by holdings with too big discounts," Stefan Casteleyn of Antwerp brokerage Corluy & Co said.
